extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners, respondents in USPTO disciplinary proceedings, and USPTO enforcement staff
extracted.subtask_description: Final Order documenting exclusion from practice before the USPTO under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24 based on reciprocal discipline (state disbarment), describing procedural service, publication, prohibitions during exclusion, and reinstatement obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reciprocal discipline under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Exclusion from practice before the USPTO may be imposed pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24 when a practitioner has been disbarred or otherwise disciplined by a licensing authority in a State; the USPTO Director may impose discipline identical to that imposed by the State unless the respondent establishes a genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notice and Order informed Respondent that if he seeks to contest imposition of exclusion, he must file, within 40 days, a response containing all information sufficient to establish a genuine issue of material fact that imposition of identical discipline would be unwarranted based on grounds permissible under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1). Failure to file a timely response supports a determination that no genuine issue exists and that exclusion is appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service and notice procedures (mailing and publication) under USPTO rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Notice and Order and any Supplemental Order are to be mailed (first-class certified mail, return receipt requested) to addresses provided by the respondent and to any address where the OED Director reasonably believes the respondent receives mail; if mailed service fails, service by publication pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(b) and § 11.35(b) may be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order documents attempted mailings to Bend and Sisters, Oregon, returned as 'not deliverable' and 'unclaimed.' A Supplemental Order reset response time and was mailed; when mailings failed, service by publication was published in the Official Gazette (dates given). The publication notice informed Respondent how to obtain copies by written request to the USPTO General Counsel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 while excluded
rubrics_metrics.description: While excluded from practice before the Office, the respondent must comply fully with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order grants the respondent limited recognition to practice for 30 days from the date the Final Order is signed solely to facilitate compliance with the provisions of 37 C.F.R. § 11.58(b). The requirement to comply 'fully' indicates ongoing obligations (e.g., winding down client matters, notifying clients) described in § 11.58.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissociation and prohibition on USPTO customer numbers and PKI certificates
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO shall promptly dissociate the respondent's name from all USPTO customer numbers and public key infrastructure (PKI) certificates; the respondent shall not use or obtain any USPTO customer number or PKI certificate unless and until reinstated to practice before the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an affirmative administrative action and a continuing prohibition: respondent may not use existing customer numbers/PKI or obtain new ones while excluded; reinstatement is prerequisite to regaining these privileges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and notice of discipline (Official Gazette, OED Reading Room, and notice to agencies/courts)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish the Final Order and a Notice of Exclusion in the Official Gazette and make disciplinary decisions available in the Office of Enrollment and Discipline's Reading Room; in accordance with 37 C.F.R. § 11.59, notice of public discipline and reasons must be given to state disciplinary enforcement agencies, courts where the practitioner is admitted, and the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order includes an explicit Notice of Exclusion text and cites posting location (URL) and publication dates; it requires affirmative outreach by the OED Director to relevant agencies and courts pursuant to § 11.59.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement obligations under 37 C.F.R. § 11.60
rubrics_metrics.description: Any request for reinstatement to practice before the USPTO must comply fully with 37 C.F.R. § 11.60.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order states Respondent shall comply fully with § 11.60 upon any request for reinstatement, indicating procedural and substantive requirements in § 11.60 govern eligibility and process for reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantive misconduct findings supporting discipline (state charges listed)
rubrics_metrics.description: The reasons given for the respondent's state resignation/disbarment include: neglecting legal matters entrusted to a lawyer; failing to keep clients reasonably informed and failing to promptly comply with reasonable requests for information; failing to explain matters to the extent reasonably necessary to permit clients to make informed decisions regarding the representation; failing to deposit and maintain client funds in trust; failing to account for client funds; failing to promptly deliver funds and other property clients are entitled to receive; failing to withdraw when continued representation will result in violation of disciplinary rules; failing to comply with obligations on termination of representation; dishonesty—conversion of client funds; misrepresentation; and failing to respond to lawful requests of a disciplinary authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These listed misconducts were the basis for the state proceeding and informed the USPTO's reciprocal discipline. They exemplify the types of ethical violations that, if established by a state disciplinary authority, will support USPTO exclusion absent successful contest under § 11.24(d)(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory and regulatory authority for USPTO discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: This action is taken pursuant to the provisions of 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32, and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.24 and 11.59.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Citing the statutory/regulatory basis clarifies the Office's authority to impose reciprocal discipline, publish notice, and notify other agencies; practitioners should refer to these provisions for detailed legal authority and procedures.
